text: Welcome to week 11 of the official
NASCAR Gen 4 Cup series. And this week,
you'll be heading to Darlington Raceway
for 85 laps.
This week, you'll want to use your
warm-up and first time laps to heat up
your tires and find your reference
points for your final lap. This pavement
is slick through the corners, so it
would be in your best interests to roll
around and check your marks. Turn two
will be especially difficult on a fast
lap, so be sure to double check your
ideal line through the exit, as most
laps will come to an end there as a
result of an early apex or late turn
down the track.
As you hit turns three and four, roll up
the track, figure out where your right
rear sits, and roll onto the throttle as
you take the white flag. It's very easy
to slide up in turn one, so you want to
lift and drag the brakes where the track
dips into the corner and apex right
where the flat meets the banking. Ease
back onto the gas as soon as you feel
the car set through the center. Carry
speed as you let the car ride up the
track and get the nose pointed back
down. Apex where the rubber covers the
white lines and ride the right rear onto
the backstretch. Break for turn three
between the painted portions of the wall
and point the car toward the bottom
lines. Let it roll as you continue
carrying speed and build off of it as
you point the nose back down the track.
Get on the throttle and exit turn four
to finish your lap.

You'll be starting the race gingerly in
second gear. And before you get up to
speed, you'll be faced with your first
challenge, turn one, two by two. While a
zipper merge giving way to the cars on
the inside would be ideal, this is a
race. If you find yourself side by side
with someone heading into turn one, not
only at the initial start, but over the
course of the entire race, keep in mind
who's ahead before the breaking point
and who's most likely to slide up past
the apex. It is possible to take turns
one and two double file, but your
success will rely on both drivers
abilities to enter low enough that
neither of them slide up the track and
into the closest obstacle. Not only will
it be difficult, but it will also cost
you a lot of time and potentially stack
up the field to cause a wreck. In order
to survive here, let alone win the race,
you will need to learn when to cut your
losses. Once you get single file and
continue on with your race, your passes
will most likely be made at the exits of
the corners. It may be tempting to shove
it down the inside going into turn
three, but with how slick the track will
be, your right front tire would pay the
price. To avoid this, you want to run a
diamond, entering around the second
lane, trail breaking as the car rolls up
the track, and pitching the car back
down towards the dotted white lines on
exit. If you hit this properly as the
run goes on, you'll find the car
pivoting well on exit, offering you
additional speed on the cars ahead of
you.
I ran 25 laps around the traditional
line and the car started tight, trended
tight, and was still tight by the end of
the run. I felt that I was taking it
easy on my right front as the run went
on, but my wear would suggest that I
could have backed off my entries more
and allowed the car to roll slightly
longer through the centers. It's because
it's so easy to burn off the right front
that I advise against passing on the
inside here. It's easy to overshoot the
corners and get into the wall without
help. But if you pin yourself against
the bottom any longer than you need to,
you'll only be asking for trouble once
tires become a factor. With a fuel
window of 58 to 63 laps, you'll be
guaranteed a single fuel stop. And as
far as tires are concerned, you'll
likely be better off taking all four
this week. Unless you find yourself with
a short run to the end. The left sides
wear as if the car was trending loose.
So there is a slight chance you could
get away with it. With how bad the wheel
spin will be on the restarts, taking all
four and getting ready to dodge the
upcoming crash would likely be your best
strategy.
If you can keep yourself out of the
wall, measure your risks, and keep your
right side tires under you, you could
find yourself loading the car into the
hauler in one piece. Good luck.
